html:
SMTO-TSK-0001 — This task is waiting on other work that hasn't finished

GUID: a35936aa-6262-4d39-8bca-7551b32673fb
Slug: dependency-resource-blocked
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • SMTO can't move this task forward yet because work it depends on is stuck or still running, or an earlier task in this conversation is still going. Nothing new was started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the task's activity and look for steps marked as blocked or waiting. Read the reason shown under each one. The blocked step says what it's waiting for, such as something another task is still using.
  2. If an earlier task in this conversation is still running, wait for it to finish, or stop it if you no longer need it. Tasks in one conversation take turns, so this one can only continue after the earlier one ends.
  3. If a step is waiting on something that will never finish, select Stop on that step or Stop task. Stopping it lets the task end cleanly instead of waiting forever.
  4. Before continuing, check whether the stopped steps had already changed anything, then select Resume or Restart task. Some blocked steps may have partly run, and repeating them could do the work twice.

What success looks like

  • The task's status changes from blocked or waiting to running, and new steps appear in its activity.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the conversation to clear the block; it holds the record of what already ran.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Completion is blocked because dependency activities remain pending on unresolved resources, or a continuation or retry is ineligible because its dependencies are unsatisfied, its status does not allow it, or an earlier task holds the conversation lane.

What this means

  • Dependency completion still has pending resource-blocked activities, or lane continuation cannot acquire eligibility behind existing authoritative work. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • Dependency completion still has pending resource-blocked activities, or lane continuation cannot acquire eligibility behind existing authoritative work.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the named dependency/resource owner and the current lane's continuation eligibility; a blocked task is not necessarily dead.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the task's dependency state and the activities in blocked_resource or pending states (dependency_graph.completion_gate), or the lane's open task and dependency evaluation (reserve_chat_attempt, recovery_unavailable). Wait for, stop or reconcile the owning work using the existing activity and scheduler controls, then continue; preserve original receipts and reconcile possible effects before new work.
  • Inspect the current blocker and wait, release or reconcile it using the existing scheduler controls.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Existing owners and dependencies settle and normal scheduling makes the intended task eligible.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
